INTERNAL — Sales/SE/CS enablement handout

What this is
- A one-page guide to using Redwood’s new Latency/$ Benchmark Report in discovery, outbound, and POCs.
- Goal: consistent talk track + safe claims + clean CTA paths (trial vs demo vs Dedicated sizing).

TL;DR (what changed)
- We published a production-focused benchmark report and interactive benchmark table centered on inference economics.
- Primary metric: “latency per dollar” (Latency/$), with supporting views for p50/p95 latency, throughput, and estimated cost per 1M tokens.
- The methodology is documented and reproducible (prompt set, prefill/decode mix, concurrency, warmup, caching/batching policy, and stability gates).
- Sales assets now include: interactive page, downloadable PDF, methodology explainer, and objection-handling FAQ.

Why it matters (how to position)
- Buyers aren’t just optimizing for raw tokens/sec; they’re optimizing for product SLOs + unit economics.
- Our story: Redwood helps teams make inference predictable and economical across regions and deployment modes (Hosted, Dedicated, Private).
- Use this report to anchor the conversation in real production constraints: p95 latency, variability, cost controls, and regional consistency.

Top insights to lead with (pick 1–2, don’t info-dump)
1) Economics-based comparison (not “benchmark theater”)
   - The report is designed around production-shaped workloads (not single-request, best-case microbenchmarks).
   - We show tradeoffs: Latency/$ alongside p95 latency and throughput.

2) Regional performance consistency is a feature
   - Many teams expand into EU/APAC and hit latency variance + capacity unpredictability.
   - We measured across multiple regions with repeat runs + stability gates to reduce one-off noise.

3) Dedicated and Private are the “control plane for SLOs” when usage gets serious
   - Hosted gets you to value quickly.
   - Dedicated is for predictable throughput, isolation, and tighter p95 targets.
   - Private is for regulated workloads, networking control, and audit/KMS needs.

4) Transparent caveats = higher credibility
   - We disclose what we measured, how we measured it, and where results may differ (token distribution, tool calling patterns, streaming, cache hit rate, safety layers, etc.).

Who this is for (customer fit)
- Best-fit prospects to route toward this asset:
  - AI-native or devtools teams optimizing unit economics at scale (cost-sensitive, high request volume)
  - Teams with strict product latency SLOs (especially p95) and regional users (EU/APAC)
  - Platform teams standardizing inference across business units (want consistent tooling + rollout controls)
  - Regulated or security-driven orgs evaluating VPC/on-prem (need an audit-friendly story + reproducibility)

- Less ideal / needs careful framing:
  - Prospects demanding “your number must exactly match my app” without running a PoC
  - Workloads dominated by unique long-context prompts with near-zero cache reuse (still possible, but talk about expected deltas)

Recommended CTA paths (choose one)
1) PLG / Hosted-first
   - CTA: “Start a free trial and reproduce results on your top 3 prompts.”
   - When to use: early stage, dev-led buyers, quick time-to-value.
   - Offer: quickstart + sample harness + link to methodology.

2) Sales-assisted / Dedicated sizing
   - CTA: “Let’s do a Dedicated sizing call based on your concurrency + context length distribution.”
   - When to use: they care about p95, have predictable volume, or need isolation/commit.
   - What to ask for: expected QPS, concurrency, prefill/decode mix, regions, target p95, peak/burst patterns.

3) Security/regulated / Private
   - CTA: “Book a Private/VPC architecture + security review.”
   - When to use: data residency, audit logging, KMS/HSM, regulated environments.
   - Attach: methodology + redaction statement + security review packet (coordinate with Naomi Feldman / Security).

How to talk about the benchmark (safe talk track)
- 15-second opener:
  “We published a production-focused benchmark report that compares inference economics across models and regions using a reproducible methodology. The core metric is Latency/$—a way to understand both speed and cost together—backed by p50/p95 latency and throughput so you can map results to your SLOs.”

- One sentence that earns trust:
  “We also publish the ‘how we measured’ details and call out where your workload might differ—so you can reproduce and validate it for your prompts.”

What NOT to say (disallowed/avoid)
- “Fastest in the world” / “best overall” / blanket superiority claims.
- “This will match your production latency exactly.”
- Unqualified competitor callouts (“X is slow/expensive”) without the approved caveats and legal-reviewed language.

Common questions + crisp answers
Q: Is this cherry-picked?
A: No—workloads are defined up front, runs include warmup, fixed concurrency settings, and stability gates. We publish methodology and rerun criteria.

Q: Does caching/batching help the numbers?
A: The report specifies the caching/batching policy. We’ll walk through what was enabled and how that might change with your cache hit rate and traffic patterns.

Q: Why Latency/$ instead of tokens/sec?
A: Tokens/sec alone can hide cost tradeoffs and SLO risk. Latency/$ is an economics-forward view; we still provide p95 latency and throughput for completeness.

Q: Can customers reproduce?
A: Yes—use the published methodology and we can provide a PoC plan to run the same prompt mix and concurrency against your target regions.

Field checklist (discovery prompts)
- Regions: where are users? (NA/EU/APAC split)
- SLO: p95 latency target and tail tolerance
- Context length distribution (typical + worst case)
- Concurrency profile (average vs peak)
- Response style: streaming vs non-streaming, tool/function calling frequency
- Cost constraints: target $/1M tokens (or monthly budget for inference)
- Deployment constraints: data residency, VPC requirements, on-prem/air-gapped needs

Where to find the assets (internal)
- Interactive benchmark page (public): use in calls + follow-up email
- PDF report: attach for exec-friendly summary
- Methodology page: send when asked “how did you measure?”
- Sales FAQ + objection handling: use for competitor/fairness questions

Owners / escalation
- Messaging/positioning: Soojin Lee (PMM)
- Technical methodology questions: Jonas Weber / Claire Dubois (Applied ML & Evals)
- Reproducibility / PoC harness guidance: Markus Klein (Solutions Engineering)
- Legal/comparative claims: Michael Grant / Sofia Mendes

Version notes
- This one-pager is aligned to the launch materials as of 2025-07-16. If a model list/region coverage changes, request an updated talk track before sending new claims externally.
